text: mcp model divides change-point variable \(x\) \(K\) segments separated ordered change points \(\tau_1 < \dots < \tau_{K-1}\). segment \(k \\{1, \dots, K\}\), linear predictor \(\eta_i\) measures \(x\) change point \(\tau_{k-1}\): $$\eta_i = \alpha_k + \beta_{k,1} (x_i - \tau_{k-1}) \quad (\text{} \tau_0 = 0)$$ \(\alpha_k\) value start segment \(k\): $$\alpha_k = \begin{cases}   \beta_{k,0}, & \text{disjoined } (\sim \texttt{1 + x}, \text{ } k = 1) \\   \alpha_{k-1} + \beta_{k-1,1} (\tau_{k-1} - \tau_{k-2}), & \text{joined } (\sim \texttt{0 + x}) \end{cases}$$ , disjoined segment starts intercept \(\beta_{k,0}\), joined segment continues segment \(k-1\) left . , \(\beta_{k,1}\) slope \(x\) segment \(k\). Intercepts slopes absolute values (changes relative preceding segments). variables (e.g., + z + state) add \(\sum_j \gamma_{k,j} z_{j,}\) segments included. use original values part \(\alpha_k\), can make joined segment start jump. inverse-linked parameter \(\mu_i = g^{-1}(\eta_i)\) via link function \(g(\mu_i) = \eta_i\), representing expected response families (success probability binomial models, expected count \(n_i \mu_i\)). Distributional parameters (sigma(), shape(), etc.) autoregressive terms (ar(), ma()) follow exact segmented structure respective link scales. Since segmented linear predictor, mcp calls distributional parameters (dpar): mu, sigma, shape, AR/MA lag (ar1, ar2, ma1, ...), e.g., fitted(fit, dpar = "ar1") fixef(fit, dpar = "sigma"). See details mcp website.

title: Model formulas in mcp — mcp-formula
text: Autoregressive (ar(p)) moving-average (ma(q)) terms define finite conditional recurrence link scale (generalized autoregressive moving-average, GARMA). support Gaussian (identity), binomial (logit), Bernoulli (logit), Poisson (log), negative-binomial (log) families. \(\eta^{\text{reg}}_t\) ordinary regression predictor segment formulas \(\eta_t\) predictor including serial dependence, recurrence decomposes components: $$\begin{aligned}   \text{AR}_t &= \sum_{j=1}^{p} \phi_{j,t} \left[g(y^*_{t-j}) - \eta^{\text{reg}}_{t-j}\right] \\   \text{MA}_t &= \sum_{k=1}^{q} \theta_{k,t} \left[g(y^*_{t-k}) - \eta_{t-k}\right] \\   \eta_t &= \eta^{\text{reg}}_t + \text{AR}_t + \text{MA}_t \end{aligned}$$ \(\phi_{j,t}\) lag-\(j\) autoregressive (AR) coefficient time \(t\), \(\theta_{k,t}\) lag-\(k\) moving-average (MA) coefficient time \(t\), \(g(\cdot)\) link function, \(y^*_t\) threshold-constrained observation threshold constant \(c\) (set via argument threshold = 0.1 ar() / ma()) keep residuals finite link scale: Gaussian: \(y^*_t = y_t\). Poisson / Negative Binomial: \(y^*_t = \max(y_t, c)\) prevent \(\log(0)\). \(c\) replaces zero counts small positive threshold value. Binomial / Bernoulli: \(y^*_t = \min(\max(y_t, c), n_t - c) / n_t\), \(y_t\) observed successes, \(n_t\) number trials (\(n_t = 1\) Bernoulli), \(c\) constrains counts interval \([c, n_t - c]\) converting rate, preventing \(\text{logit}(0)\) \(\text{logit}(1)\). Implications: \(N\)-order component, last \(N\) values segment's change point input first \(\eta_t\) segment. AR MA components apply segments included. AR coefficients jointly constrained stationarity; MA coefficients invertibility. See arma article details.

sampled as the value at the segment end #>   Intercept_3 = Intercept_3_end_ - (time_3 * (cp_3 - cp_2)) #>   time_3 ~ dnorm(0, 1/(0.62123709509255609)^2)   # Autoscaled mean coefficient (rstanarm default) #>   sigma_1 ~ dt(0, 1/(5.7)^2, 3) T(0,)  # Positive residual SD calibrated on the response scale #>  #>   # Model and likelihood #>   for (i_ in 1:length(time)) { #>     # par_x local to each segment #>     x_local_1_[i_] = min(time[i_], cp_1) #>     x_local_2_[i_] = min(time[i_], cp_2) - cp_1 #>     x_local_3_[i_] = min(time[i_], cp_3) - cp_2 #>      #>     # Formula for mu #>     link_mu_[i_] = #>       (time[i_] >= cp_0) * (time[i_] < cp_2) * inprod(rhs_matrix_[i_, c(1)], c(Intercept_1)) * 1 +  #>       (time[i_] >= cp_1) * (time[i_] < cp_2) * inprod(rhs_matrix_[i_, c(2)], c(time_2)) * x_local_2_[i_] +  #>       (time[i_] >= cp_2) * inprod(rhs_matrix_[i_, c(3)], c(Intercept_3)) * 1 +  #>       (time[i_] >= cp_2) * inprod(rhs_matrix_[i_, c(4)], c(time_3)) * x_local_3_[i_] #>      #>     # Formula for sigma #>     link_sigma_[i_] = #>       (time[i_] >= cp_0) * inprod(rhs_matrix_[i_, c(5)], c(sigma_1)) * 1 #>  #>     # Likelihood for family = gaussian() #>     mu_[i_] = link_mu_[i_] #>     sigma_[i_] = max(1e-05, link_sigma_[i_]) #>     response[i_] ~ dnorm(mu_[i_], 1 / sigma_[i_]^2) #>   } #> } # }

title: mcp 0.4.0
text: Multiple regression: mcp now supports several continuous predictors, categorical predictors, interactions, etc. terms RHS. E.g., ~ 1 + x + x:state + sigma(1 + state) + ar(2, 0 + z). Basically, now aims “feels” like lm() glm() distributional parameter segment. Explore ex = mcp_example("multiple") see action. Default priors follow rstanarm brms possible. possibility parameters also comes convenient () share coefficients across segments - including categorical predictors group-level effects. Group-level effects RHS: Predictor formulas now support group-level effects (random effects) using familiar lme4 brms syntax. (1 | group) specifies group-level intercept, (1 + x || group) (factor || group) support independent coefficients, including slopes factors. also works inside distributional formulas sigma(1 + (factor || id)). See mcp_example("group_mu") worked example. Correlated multi-coefficient terms yet supported. Native feel: mcpfits now work natively R generics, posterior tidybayes posterior draw prediction API. Changes include: summary(fit) now reports rank-normalized split-rhat, ess_bulk, ess_tail posterior central quantile intervals instead HDIs. Adding as_draws(fit), as_draws_df(fit), tidy_draws(fit), ndraws(fit), posterior_epred(fit), posterior_predict(fit), posterior_linpred(fit), loo_compare(), etc. full S3 generic registration posterior, rstantools, tidybayes (spread_draws(), gather_draws()). bayesplot::mcmc_trace(fit) etc. work now. Per-draw methods (summary = FALSE fitted(), predict(), residuals(), log_lik()) now return dot-prefixed columns (.epred, .prediction, .residual, .loglik) tidybayes / ggdist compatibility. fitted() returns .linpred scale = "linear" [.dpar] dpars (e.g., .sigma, .ar1, mu). nsamples soft-deprecated favor ndraws; which_y deprecated favor dpar. Added R generics mcpfits: formula(fit), family(fit), model.frame(fit), nobs(fit), vcov(fit), confint(fit). Fits now also store proper matched $call. Printed summaries now report posterior sd new layout. Dirichlet now default prior change points: default change point prior now mathematically beautiful principled dirichlet(1) (flat Dirichlet / uniform order statistics). Effectively, prior remain unchanged models 1 change point Dirichlet reduces uniform prior. models 2+ change points, previous “truncated-t” prior removed. served purpose higher ESS/s expense mathematically unprincipled. previous mcp versions supported slow implementation Dirichlet, achieving good ESS/s made possible sampling dirichlet(1) sorted uniforms (dirichlet(alpha) use sequential stick-breaking Beta chain, z_j \sim \text{Beta}(\alpha, (N - j + 1) \alpha)). Comparing mcp_example(), estimates remain essentially identical truncated-t dirichlet. hypothesis(fit, "cp_1 = 20") (Savage-Dickey Bayes Factor) default priors likely differ, BF ill advised default priors anyway - hypothesis() throws warning attempted. Read mcp website. Negative binomial offset(): can now mcp(..., family = negbinomial()). NB (Poisson) can now model rates exposure offset() now supported formulas - also families. one segment includes offset(), segments must include one. Missing response imputation: Missing responses now retained posterior JAGS imputations used complete response histories AR/MA models. Predictions generate fresh replicated outcomes every row; predict(fit) |> filter(.na(y)) can used see predictive intervals draws missing points, similarly fitted() expected responses. Missing AR/MA histories remain unsupported log_lik(), loo(), waic(). Improved speed robustness: ESS/s improved 10-fold convergence likely. due reparameterizations keep intercepts slopes relatively independent earlier segments sampling due (selectively) using JAGS glm module. reparameterizations change model priors. Compare fit$jags_code options(mcp_reparam = FALSE) (plain model) options(mcp_reparam = TRUE) (default). Read formulas sampler code.

title: mcp 0.4.0
text: mcp v0.4 major breaking change aim remaining relatively stable going forward towards version 1.0. Although lot updated, parameter estimates v0.4.0 remain practically identical previous public release (v0.3.4). Deprecation detections added reach 1.0. Renamed parameters column names align brms: int_i –> Intercept_i; x_1_E2 –> xE2_1; x_1_sin –> sinx_1, cp_1_sd –> cp_1_id_sd ((1 | id)), etc. Interactions join parts dot, e.g., x:stateB –> x.stateB_1. Renamed return column names align posterior others: summary(), fixef(), ranef() now name parameter identifier column parameter instead name, matching prior_summary() mcp_pars(). fitted(), predict(), residuals(), log_lik() summary = TRUE now take width = 0.95 instead probs (deprecated warning) return columns .mean, .sd, .lower, .upper instead fitted/predict/residuals/loglik, error, Q2.5, Q97.5. matches summary() (width, mean, sd, lower, upper), dot prefix prevents collisions data columns, broom::augment(). Consequently, data columns named sd, fitted, predict, etc. longer rejected. quantiles, summarise draws summary = FALSE. evaluation-row key data_row now .data_row. Rhat renamed rhat summary(), fixef(), ranef(), match posterior standard. hypothesis() returns column prob instead p posterior (prior) probability directional hypotheses, preventing confusion frequentist p-values. also returns posterior sd hypothesis, like summary(). Change points modeled using cp(): Segments 2+ now one-sided formulas, change points modeled using cp(), e.g., list(y ~ 1, ~ cp((1 | id)) + 0 + x) instead list(y ~ 1, 1 + (1 | id) ~ 0 + x). avoids confusing left-hand side response variable. old syntax deprecated works warning shows new formula. formula(fit) summary(fit) show new syntax. Parameters outputs: fit$pars fit$mcmc_loglik removed now raises helpful errors. fit$pars now replaced mcp_pars(fit) mcp_columns(fit). fit$mcmc_loglik longer stored - generate using log_lik(fit). mcp:::tidy_samples() removed. Use as_draws_df(fit) tidybayes::spread_draws(). fixef() now reports population-level effects mu (primary response parameter), excluding change points, distributional parameters, AR/MA parameters, group-effect SDs. Use summary(fit) get parameters. general, renamed "varying" "group", e.g., now plot_pars(fit, pars = "group") fitted(fit, group_effects = "x_2_id"). varying deprecated alias warning. summary(), fixef(), ranef(), prior_summary(), as_draws(), fit$prior, fit$simulate(), everything else now order parameters canonically mcp_pars() instead previous incidental (near-alphabetical) order; group levels follow grouping factor’s levels fitting data. Draws fitted(), predict(), etc. summary = FALSE ordered data row, draw, tidybayes. Use verbose = TRUE summary(), fixef(), ranef() include segment dpar columns. Tibbles generally returned instead data.frame() readability. Tibbles data frames, x[, "col"] now returns one-column tibble instead vector. Use x$col x[["col"]] get vector. change involves summary(), fixef(), ranef(), fitted(), predict(), residuals(), hypothesis(), interpolate_newdata(). mcp longer exports phi, logit, ilogit, probit. Functions, plotting, workflow: plot() now split plot() plotting full fits plot_dpar() plots one distributional parameter (mu, sigma, shape, ar1, etc.). argument order changed . new coloring function (plot(fit, color_by = "column")) particularly useful models include categorical predictors rhs group-level effects. default color_by = "auto" colors sole categorical predictor. See mcp_example("group_mu") worked example. Parallel sampling now controlled exclusively active future plan. cores argument mcp() deprecated ignored, remains available backwards compatibility. Use future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 3) calling mcp() sample chains parallel, future::plan(future::sequential) shut workers. Without parallel future plan, chains sampled sequentially. Chain-specific initial values (inits = list(list(...), list(...))) now supported parallel execution supplying explicit seed. Binomial predictions now default counts: fitted() returns expected successes predict() returns predicted successes (rate = FALSE), matching posterior_epred(), posterior_predict(), brms. v0.3.4 methods defaulted proportions. Update old scripts explicit rate = TRUE retain proportions, rate = FALSE select counts. omitted rate warns per session per function requested counts differ proportions. ar(p) longer continues later segments: terms included segment get coefficients . important new multiple-regression functionality, backward incompatibility model like model = list(y ~ 1 + ar(1), ~ 0), AR continue segment 2. equivalent model v0.4+ ~ 0 + ar(1, 0) segment 2. Explicit prior draw selection: Methods requiring draws now require posterior draws default error unavailable. Use prior = TRUE select prior draws; prior-fits longer trigger automatic fallback. also applies draw-count methods, print(fit) shows model unless prior = TRUE. arguments fit$simulate() changed accommodate multiple (categorical) predictors. fit$simulate(fit, newdata, ..., .type = "predict") new argument structure. Note (1) now requires fit first argument, (2) requires data.frame tibble second argument instead just vector par_x, (3) arguments prefixed “.” avoid name conflicts internally mcp. ... model parameters usual. fit$simulate() now also preserve shared group effects specified priors (e.g., prior = list(Intercept_2_id = "Intercept_1_id")). hypothesis() takes fit first argument x (fit), matching brms::hypothesis(). now restricts equality tests simple parameter contrasts gives clearer guidance Savage-Dickey Bayes factors. Non-linear transformations hypotheses like x_1 / x_2 = 1 previously run, even though Savage-Dickey support . Equality tests now return prob = NA Bayes factor model comparison, posterior parameter probability. Density estimates robust, warn evaluating Savage-Dickey Bayes factors default priors, warn sparse tails. mcp(..., adapt = 1000) soft-deprecated favor mcp(..., warmup = 1000) compatibility additional future samplers. Formula modeling semantics: Dropped support rel() formulas. ambiguous interaction terms made code hard maintain. Another way achieving functionality via priors may added future versions. Dropped support mcp(..., data = NULL). now must provide mock-data inform mcp types levels predictor columns. See, e.g., mcp_example("intercepts")$example_code simple example mcp_example("multiple")$example_code involved example. docs updated appropriately. Gaussian models explicit sigma() formula now model residual standard deviation log link, brms. make scale visible, intercepts named sigma_Intercept_i (previously sigma_i), matching Intercept_i, slopes keep names (e.g., sigma_x_2) now log scale. Models without explicit sigma() unchanged: sigma_1 remains residual SD response-scale half-Student-t prior. y | weights(w) now specifies observation log-likelihood weights rather Gaussian-precision weights (previously scaled residual SD sigma / sqrt(w)). Unlike brms, weights must strictly positive due JAGS requirements (zero). Predictive draws expectations now use distribution parameters directly log_lik() multiplies observation log-densities w. title: mcp 0.4.0

Explicit AR/MA prediction history control: predict() new posterior_predict() support conditional = TRUE (default) condition observed response histories, conditional = FALSE generate histories recursively. applies prior posterior prediction. Previously, AR history handling depended whether response values supplied. Added AR/MA warnings: (1) AR/MA models loo(), predict(), etc. serial dependence currently ignored. Proper handling requires leave-future-blocked cross-validation, currently implemented mcp. (2) posterior violation probabilities exceed configurable ar ma diagnostic thresholds (10% default). New features mcp(): Added warnings various thresholds exceeded. mcp(..., diagnostics = list(rhat = 1.01, ess_bulk = 400, ess_tail = 400, ar = 0.10, ma = 0.10)) controls fit diagnostics configurable thresholds. Partial lists override defaults, individual diagnostics can disabled NULL, diagnostics = FALSE disables diagnostic warnings. summary(fit) inherits settings accepts override diagnostic footer. Use mcp(..., seed = 42) set.seed(42) mcp() reproducible JAGS sampling, whether chains run sequentially parallel. See mcp_example("demo")$example_code ensure reproducibility across simulation, fit, plotting. mcp(..., quiet = TRUE) suppresses routine JAGS output mcp sampling-status messages preserving warnings errors. Use options(mcp_quiet = TRUE) make default session. JAGS model-compilation text longer printed default. Memory improvement: mcpfit now < 10% size log-likelihood stored. Use log_lik(fit) compute , call loo(fit) waic(fit) directly. Methods like fitted() predict() now select group-level effects using group_effects (previously varying). group_effects = FALSE NA gives population-level predictions, "cp" "predictor" select group-level effects formula part, parameter names accept * wildcards, e.g., fitted(fit, group_effects = c("cp_*", "state*_1_id")). ranef() continues return group-level effects. Fits made custom jags_code now warn calling R-side simulation, prediction, model-evaluation methods, methods continue evaluate supplied formulas rather custom JAGS code. Priors hypotheses: Added prior_summary(fit). compact output shows parameter’s resolved prior bounds; prior_summary(fit, verbose = TRUE) also shows data-dependent rule, plain-language description, source, kind (distribution, alias, expression, constant). introduction multiple regression including categorical predictors (including distributional parameters) come default priors. Coefficients autoscaled rstanarm, .e., divided SD model-matrix column (see “Priors distributions” ). See prior_summary(fit, verbose = TRUE) details. Added option test hypotheses prior using hypothesis(fit, prior = TRUE). y | weights(w_col) now supported families (gaussian(), binomial(), bernoulli(), poisson(), negbinomial()). Applies log-likelihood weights brms. Plotting examples: Default plot(fit) style updated many ways accommodate multiple regression group-effects. Predictive intervals (plot(fit, q_predict = TRUE) predict(fit, summary = TRUE)) now precise faster. used estimated posterior parameter draws, MC error. Added interpolate_newdata(fit, = NULL) generates data.frame combinations categorical predictors along interpolated continuous predictors. Use include grouping factors. documentation shows can useful generating custom plots simple tweaking plot() enough. mcp_example(...) now shows illustrative plot fitted example default. Disable using plot = FALSE. New help topics ?mcp-formula (model formulas underlying model) ?mcp-priors (prior syntax), split ?mcp.

title: mcp 0.4.0
text: Priors distributions: Default coefficient priors now follow autoscaled defaults rstanarm: normal(0, 2.5 * sd(y) / sd(x)) identity links normal(0, 2.5 / sd(x)) log links, sd(x) standard deviation predictor’s model-matrix column, including dummy variables factors. change-point variable, sd(x) taken data (slope priors depend number change points), powers (x^2) use sd((x - min(x))^2), interactions x:z use sd(x) * sd(z) (just sd(x) 0/1 dummies x:state). Version 0.3.4 used dt(0, sd(y) / (max(x) - min(x)), 3) Gaussian slopes, 9 times narrower evenly spread x noticeably shrank steep slopes short segments. Intercepts also follow rstanarm (normal(mean(y), 2.5 * sd(y)) Gaussian models), default prior segment-1 intercept applies level min(x), just rstanarm brms place intercept priors centered predictors. Intercept_1 still reported x = 0, lm(), fit$prior prior_summary() show prior given x-terms, e.g., normal(mean = mean(y) - x_1 * min(x), sd = 2.5 * sd(y)). greatly improves sampling x far zero, e.g., calendar years. Likewise factor levels contrasts x-terms, e.g., stateb_1 y ~ 1 + state * x. sigma group-level SDs follow brms. See priors using prior_summary(fit, verbose = TRUE). implicit Gaussian sigma_1 prior now response-calibrated half-Student-t used brms, dt(0, max(2.5, round(mad(y), 1)), 3) T(0, ). Version 0.3.4 instead used response-SD-calibrated half-normal prior. weakly informative negligible impact fits. Uppercase data-dependent constants priors (MINX, MAXX, etc.) remain temporarily supported deprecation warning. now replaced readable expressions min(time), max(time) - min(time), mad(response), n_segments(), n_cp(). Binomial Bernoulli models logit probit links now use narrower, weakly regularizing scales rstanarm’s 2.5: normal(0, 1.5) (logit) normal(0, 1) (probit) intercepts, approximately exactly uniform probability scale, respectively. Coefficients categorical contrasts use normal(0, 1.5 / sd(x)) normal(0, 1 / sd(x)). Gaussian models log link (gaussian(link = "log")): Now aligned mcp’s general log-link model standards (dnorm rather Student-t reduce extreme multiplicative tails exponentiation). Population intercepts robustly calibrated empirical log-data (non-positive values replaced 0.1, brms zeros) shift offset(), coefficients categorical contrasts use rstanarm’s dnorm(0, 2.5 / sd(x)). Count model priors (poisson(), negbinomial()): v0.3.4, log-link Poisson models used uncalibrated, unscaled dnorm(0, 10) intercepts slopes. v0.4.0, population log-mean intercepts now robustly data-calibrated dnorm(median(log(y)), ...) (zeros replaced 0.1, brms) minimum scale 2.5, automatically shift observed log-rate (\log(y) - \text{offset}) offset() present (calibrating location scale directly rates, unlike brms, subtracts mean(offset) location computes scale log-counts). Coefficients categorical contrasts now use rstanarm’s dnorm(0, 2.5 / sd(x)). new RHS group-level features v0.4.0, group SDs default dnorm(0, 2.5) T(0, ) (scaled half-normals). Broad normal priors follow precedent rstanarm, substantially reducing extreme multiplicative effects explosive prior simulations compared Student-t priors exponentiation. Similarly, modeled log-shape negative-binomial (shape(...)) uses dnorm(0, 2.5) dnorm(0, 2.5 / sd(x)) rather Student-t priors. Interface data structures: fit = mcp_example("name") now returns fit directly instead list $fit entry. now defaults sampling model (sample = "post") sample argument now directly passed mcp(..., sample = sample) sample = TRUE deprecated. term “ct” (“central tendency”) replaced dpar = "epred" (default), e.g., plot_dpar(fit, dpar = "epred") fitted(fit, dpar = "epred"). Deprecated which_y = "ct" translated dpar = "epred" warning. mcp(..., inits) can set stochastic nodes fit$jags_code. Change points (e.g., cp_1) parameters reparameterized faster sampling can longer initialized directly. fit$data now contains data columns used model. draws_format replaces samples_format fitted(), predict(), log_lik(). old argument remains available soft deprecation. residuals() now also takes draws_format, e.g., residuals(fit, summary = FALSE, draws_format = "matrix") draws--observation matrix like brms. Removed which_y argument predict(). loo() waic() always evaluate fitted model, including group-level effects AR/MA terms. Use log_lik(fit, group_effects = FALSE) log_lik(fit, arma = FALSE) conditional log-likelihoods. Additionally, loo(ndraws = ...) now thins draws evenly across chains preserve MCMC chain identities order. New mcpfit objects longer include empty $loo $waic components. .mcpfit() deprecated favor is_mcpfit(), matching posterior’s is_draws(). Requirements removals: mcp now requires R >= 4.1.0, matching use native pipe (|>). Removed non-functional exponential() family. default priors fitted. Exponential survival models require dedicated support censoring survival likelihoods rather previous ordinary-response placeholder.
